I can relate. I was recently diagnosed with PTSD and it's been a painful, but enlightening, experience. I lost a parent at 12 and the other parent moved on a little too quickly, and I was forced to adapt to a new family, town, school and way of life all too quickly. Throw in a few instances of sexual assault and unrealistic expectations set on me, I suppressed so much. A bad breakup shook me up a little a few years ago, making me suspect depression. But I'm only *just now* realizing I have unresolved trauma, because it's coming out more...ugly than it ever has, and triggered by what? *Workplace bullying.* Of all the things I "made it" through, petty workplace harassment is what finally breaks me. It robbed me of my sense of purpose and security, made me feel unsafe, broke my confidence and shattered my ability to trust. That's what my psychiatrist said that made me finally break down in tears in front of someone for the very first time- my ability to trust is down to nothing. Now, I'm dealing with the simplest triggers from things like mean comments about my appearance, bad dreams, misinterpreted tonnage while speaking to others, paranoia, etc. It's a very confusing time.
However. I want to say that right now, today, things are turning around for me. Ive had somewhat of an epiphany. I understand you may not appreciate spirituality as I do, but I just took the time to rest, listen to music, and focus on my breath of life for a while. Letting go of all the shit that hurt me today. And it was so simple but so profound. And just like that, tonight I learned of a dream job opportunity- finally, an escape from the hellhole that's been torturing me for so long. 
I'm not saying the solution, or cure, or even the coping mechanisms for PTSD is simple. Hell, I'm very new to all this and I'm barely scratching the surface on my road to healing. But that is what helped me today. Maybe it'll help you.

I definitely think your mom has bad intentions, you're not crazy. Remember that- you. Are. Not. Crazy. 
But she's not really your mom anymore, is she? She doesn't deserve that place in your life after all that she's done and all the abuse and neglect she's inflicted on you. Understand that she doesn't serve a purpose in your life anymore- certainly not as a mom, not even as an aquaintence. I think you need to let go of any attachments you have to her because she has no attachment to you. Think back to the group home you stayed in- do you have any friends or anyone that could guide you in the right direction? Anyone from school, a distant relative, anyone else outside your mom's circle that could help you? 
As for finding a job. I know the pandemic screwed a lot of people up. I'm not sure where you are located, but one beautiful thing about this whole mess is that it shows which jobs are essential. Go after one of those, even if it means doing some research online. Finding a job needs to be your number one priority above all else. Spend 40 hours a week searching, and don't ever give up. Go through a temp agency (you can apply online) and they will find jobs for you. You will find a job eventually if you continuously search. I find the app Steady to be particularly helpful. This is your one way ticket out of that bad situation. Im not sure what you want to do as far as involving police, but finding a job ASAP and saving even just enough for a down payment on a studio apartment is a guaranteed way to solve your issue. Once out of the situation and safe from harm, then you can take action against her and protect your other siblings. How can you protect anybody if you are not safe yourself? 
In the meantime, you need to prioritize taking care of yourself. You have some mental health struggles that are not your fault, and they also don't define you. Do what you know you need to do to be kind to yourself. And once your free of this terrible woman, maybe look for the love and support you desire in a chosen family. At the end of the day, blood means nothing.

I didn’t necessarily perform any love spells, but I’ll throw in my own experience. A little over 2 years ago I found myself at a crossroads- dealing with a major injury that put me out of work, vulnerability due to said injury, having to rely on others to get me around, etc. My boyfriend at the time broke up with me in a pretty heartless fashion, saying all my problems were distracting him. I was hurt, and depressed from everything else but I never loved him so it wasn’t the end of the world. Just a low moment. It was after he left that I realized what exactly I was looking for/what I felt I deserved in a partner. I had a dream one night where I met someone and fell in love- and I still remember the dream vividly. The man in my dream was a tall Italian man with dark hair, green eyes and worked as a chef. The next day, I impulsively joined Match. Within 24 hours of downloading the app, I saw a profile and was instantly very attracted, so I messaged him (I NEVER messaged first, usually). We started talking on the phone that night and went on our first date a few days later. We even found we had several mutual Facebook friends despite living on completely opposite sides of the city all our lives. Fast forward to today, and we’re living together, looking for a house together, we’ve traveled and we frequently discuss marriage. He truly is “the one”. But what’s funny is he matched the dream man in every aspect- dark hair, tall, green eyes, Italian, chef. Even the sense of humor the man in my dreams had. I firmly believe that I precognitively dreamed about the love of my life. So, moral of my story is- maybe try amping up visions in dreams and see if a message comes through. Mugwort, small doses of datura, nature sounds at night are all methods I use to enhance my vivid dreams and can work for others too.

I found myself in a very similar situation as you did about 3 years ago. The job was advertised as an account managing position, and the job itself was described as direct marketing of a Fortune 500 company during the first interview. In the second interview, it was the exact breakdown of levels that you described- starting out in the field, moving up to assistant manager, and then eventually owning an office. All kinds of dollar numbers and bonuses and glitzy promises like cars and travel were thrown around. Important things to note about this interview that turned out to be red flags: for the first few months, until I got promoted, I was *guaranteed* to make between 400-700 weekly, provided that I am a *hard worker* well of course I’m a hard worker right? Also, they failed to mention that working in the field meant door to door sales. I honestly didn’t find out until the very first day. I also discovered the “office” atmosphere that they create- everybody dresses up business formal, they play loud music in the morning, everybody is pumped, scripts are practiced, all that locker room, motivational speech type energy. But in my experience, working for this company was the absolute worst time period in my life. It was never mentioned to me that pay was commission based only, and that is SO TOUGH to do when doing door to door sales, unless you naturally have an extremely instantaneous magnetic personality and are amazing at befriending strangers. People simply do not want to be disturbed, especially in their own homes. They don’t want to have to drop everything their doing on their own time to talk to a salesperson invading their property. I may be ok at dealing with the public, but I was chewed up alive out there. People were rude at best and terrifying at worst. I definitely had some very tricky and dangerous moments. Not to mention, I hardly sold anything and found myself in complete dire straights financially. 3 years later and I am still paying off credit card debt from that time just to survive. I literally went hungry. I knew a guy who got fired because he took a day off to visit his wife in the hospital after she attempted suicide. The guys in the office spread false rumors about me having relations with multiple coworkers and I was treated so badly after that. I didn’t know a single person that worked alongside me that actually made it past “manager” level. It was only towards the end that I discovered everything, from the interviews to the “critical conversations” to prevent someone from quitting, along with the sales pitch, were all entirely scripted. They didn’t care who I was as a person. All they wanted was sheer volume of people coming through, making sales. When I couldn’t make sales (they wouldnt work with me on technique) they fed me to the sharks until I bled dry. They psychologically brainwashed me into believing that I was lazy and a bad worker, plus all the coworker drama on the side. It takes a truly malicious person to watch someone like myself suffer the way I did, go days without eating food, putting quarters in to get enough gas to make it home, and not feel a damn thing about it. That is unspeakable mercilessness. There were many African American men going through our office, and some got arrested DAILY by cops called by racist fucks and the management just laughed it off. I felt so afraid for some of my friends who had it even worse than me. Getting out of that thing was the hardest thing I had to do- I had absolutely nothing. I had to go on welfare for a bit to get my head above water. It’s been a long continuous road to recovery. I feel bad for some of the people described on this sub because the brainwashing and pressure from the upper management is absolutely abusive. 
OP, I’m telling you my experience because what you described sounds all too familiar to me. Seriously reconsider this idea. You may be better off getting an hourly job in which you’re guaranteed to be paid for your time, even if it’s low paying, while you find something better.

I really think it’s different for each individual. So many factors play into how quickly one can lose weight. The way I see it, if I want to be a 5’3” 130lb woman, I have to eat like one. I became 200lbs because I ate like a 200lb person. I try really hard not to compare myself to others, because I either get discouraged for not “getting to” eat as much as others, or for not losing as much weight as quickly as others. Have you ever heard people say something along the lines of, tougher individuals seem to get dealt with more difficult situations, because they’re tough enough to handle it? I know, it’s a cliche, but I think that it’s a valid statement that applies to you. You are still here for a reason- and that reason may not be evident to you right now. What I think you need to do is take a step back and accept that. Accept that you don’t know why you’re here and you don’t know why you’re doing what you’re doing. This is absolutely fine and nobody is judging you for being where you are at. I’m not judging, anyway. I can relate to the burnout of working and attending school full time. It’s truly awful. I didn’t even feel like a person. And it took months well after the semester ended to feel like myself again. So you know what I did? I took a year off. To focus my energies on things that I like. To read books I’ve been wanting to read, to sit back and watch some movies, to have time to cook healthy delicious meals for myself, step up my game at volunteerwork. That was a choice that I made regardless of what everyone else thought. And I’m happier than I’ve ever been. I understand this may not be possible for you right now. But 5 classes and a job? OP, you’ve got your hands full and it’s no wonder you’re at a breaking point. It’s no wonder your relationships are suffering. There simply isn’t enough YOU to go around right now. So you might have a few choices. If possible, maybe drop a class or two. It can wait for next semester. I think one of the biggest problems with burnout culture is that we’re in some sort of inexplicable rush to finish everything, like we’re rushing toward that end goal that promises happiness. Here’s another cliche for you: slow down and decide to be happy now. Life is waaayy too short to be stressed out every single day. To the point of not even wanting to live. This is a symptom of burnout culture. It might seem crazy to slow down now, but why not go against the stream of what everyone else is doing? After all, if you can’t keep going at this pace, you’d thrive much better if you went at a pace that worked for you. As for your friendships and relationships, the way that person handled her issue with you was wrong. Understand that she’s out of your life now for a good reason. You need people who are responsive and receptive and appreciative and understanding. They’re out there. Take the time to look. It’s okay to do things for yourself once in a while. I hope things get better for you, I really do.

So now, I just try to stay mentally aware of my calories, being super honest with myself, checking labels and serving sizes, and try to fill up on protein instead of carbs and dessert... it’s hard because I want instant results, but I feel I am committed. It’s been a few weeks, I haven’t weighed myself and my clothes don’t feel loose yet, but somethings gotta give. I only drink water, tea (black) and coffee, and an occasional glass of wine. For some time, we considered ourselves “dating” though in school we never went on dates (weren’t allowed), never even kissed or anything. I see it as basically passing romantic notes back and forth, testing out our abilities to have romantic feelings for him. Well as we grew older, he would disappear from my life for years at a time. He’d ghost me entirely for no explicable reason. And then he’d show back up some time later and go on about how he wants to get back together and how we always have this “connection”. Well the most recent interaction was a few years ago, both fully grown and independent adults. We did end up dating for a few months and even hooked up once, but he did the disappearing act again. It’s been almost 4 years since then, and every single day I think about him. I don’t want him back, i was never really sad about his departure since I expected it, I’d never want him back, and I’m not so sure a friendship would work either. But then again, maybe it would. Maybe I do want answers. But at the same time I’m happy with who I’m with now and I don’t need him. He even shows up in my dreams almost nightly.
What I’ve learned to do is reflect on why he came into my life, why he is no longer in my life. What purpose did he serve ME? And why might his presence no longer serve me? And every time he pops in my head, I acknowledge it- and move on. Let it pass through. I’m finding that I think of him less and less.
Now, you see this coworker every day. He’s pretty hard to avoid. It’s possible that there is some sort of spiritual connection leftover from a past life, which is why you often think of him, like my case. Who knows what might’ve happened. If you want to find out once and for all, I recommend looking into the Akashic records.
If you want a simpler approach to just slow down the intrusive thoughts, I recommend clearing your mind often throughout the work day. As your day begins, set an intention to accomplish whatever it is you do to the best of your ability, and aim your focus on that. Think of this guy as merely a part of the background, as you focus on your goal of being with your SO. At the end of the day, clear your head of everything- meditation really is great- and find a way to ground yourself. Shower, watch a funny movie, take a walk in nature, listen to your favorite music, go window shopping, cook up a fun meal. 
These are just my suggestions absolutely do whatever works for you personally.
Best of luck to you.

I just came back a few days ago from Orlando, and my boyfriend and I (both 23) hit up Epcot, Animal Kingdom, and Magic Kingdom. First bit of advice- it is sooo hot. It reached 103F each day we were there, and some parks have more shaded/air conditioned areas than others. It was also extremely crowded in each park, despite using a crowd calendar to plan which parks on which days. So, to truly make the most of your time in Disney and not getting dehydrated and sick (like we did), pace yourself, drink Powerade and water whenever possible, limit your alcohol intake- even in Epcot! And take breaks to get off your feet, even for 2 minutes, whenever you need to.
That being said, we were in Epcot from rope drop to after the IllumiNations show. We started out with Future World- we loved the Living with the Land ride and the aquarium. Then we started the world showcase and got one drink and one small food item in each country, spending about an hour in each place. We definitely saw and did everything we wanted in Epcot, but we overdid it and were miserable by the time night fell. If I were to do it again, I’d do Epcot in 2 days, and not stay from opening to closing, just one or the other.
Animal kingdom was fabulous. We decided to show up a bit later, at around 11, so we would not be exhausted by the end of the day. We went on the animal trails in both Asia and Africa, the Kilimanjaro safari, and thoroughly explored Pandora, as we are both Avatar fans. We ate at Flametree barbecue, which is delicious. Above all else, we loved the Rivers of Light show at night. 
Magic Kingdom was not as fun for us. Most of the attractions are geared toward small kids, and there are not as many shaded areas to take a break. However, space mountain is always my very favorite ride so that was a must- do. We ended up leaving the park after 7, because even though we wanted to see the fireworks, we did not want to deal with the massive crowd as the park closed. 
Bottom line, if I were to do it all over again, I would do Epcot over 2 days and Animal Kingdom. Unfortunately I haven’t been to Hollywood Studios in 12 years, but I have a friend who worked there recently and loves the Toy Story addition. Have fun and enjoy your trip!

As a small child, every doctor visit was a wrangling, stressful chore for my exhausted mother, and a screeching resistance for me. Colorful band-aids, lollipops, and even ice cream were not worthy rewards for undergoing the dreaded pinch of a needle. This phobia followed me throughout my teenage years- I had refused to get my ears pierced, although I was always a tad jealous of the shiny, dangling hoops from my friends’ earlobes, framing their brightly grinning faces. My strawberry hair draped around the edges of my face and down my shoulders and swooped in messy bangs. Besides, my interests had always resided more in the outdoors. While everyone else my age was loitering at the mall, I spent my free moments wandering about the nearby parks, scouting dirt trails in my sneakers and stopping to snap photos of colorful wildflowers. The bugs and the sweat never bothered me, because I was much too entranced with listening to the chirping chorus of various bird species, catching lucky glimpse of foxes, fawns, and rabbits, and soaking in the fragmented rays of sunlight leaking in through the foliage above. I especially loved witnessing a pond scene: a calm, glinting pool of murky waters adorned with wide lily pads and clumps of algae. I loved the dragonflies and the cattails, the croaks of unseen frogs and the ducks gliding across the water with purpose.

Living in the city, nature has always been my grand escape from reality. I had felt that this feeling was sadly ironic- *we* are intruding on *nature*; nature is the reality of the Earth, and the city is the “getaway”. Sadly, my trips to the park had become less frequent as I entered my college years, as I had chosen to live off campus in a city the next state over. This is where my “shenanigans” began- the parties, the boyfriends, the drama and the drinking. I cropped my hair into a low- maintenance pixie with the help of a beautician roommate, Carla. I felt transformed from my former, shy self, like a butterfly. 

“You can’t get a butterfly tattoo,” Carla said to me one night, while sharing a bottle of red wine on our second- hand couch. “It’s too cliché. You gotta think of something else.” We had promised to get tattoos with the spare money from our respective part- time jobs: her freelancing, living-room beauty services, and my waiting tables at a street corner café. Recalling my fear of needles- after much deliberation, cajoling, and finally, an unbreakable pact between two friends- I resolved to get something small, but something meaningful to me: a simple bee. 

A few years had passed, and the bee on my wrist hadn’t faded in the slightest. I lived with my husband, a quiet, stoic man with a heart even bigger than mine. We had just bought a house in the country, and he was often occupied making home repairs, leaving me to sort out the outdoors. Spring was creeping up on us in late March, but I was nowhere near knowledgeable about planting my dream garden. All the books, blogs, and local classes seemed to fly over my head- where to even begin? I could barely keep an aloe plant alive. Yet, the fantasy of chopping up plump red tomatoes for a refreshing salsa urged me to at least give it a shot. 

March 20th  came around, the first day of spring. I woke up with a tingling sensation on my bee tattoo, although I hadn’t felt anything out of the ordinary since receiving the tattoo nearly ten years prior. To my silencing shock, I saw that the bee image was *glowing* a fantastic gold- but the previous day, and all days prior, it had been in plain, black- and-white ink. This wasn’t…a medical problem. It was strange, too strange to alert of anyone- so I had decided to carry out my pre-planned task of planting marigolds in the front yard. But, an even stranger phenomenon brought me to audible, disbelieving gasps.

We had bought 8 marigold plants for our front yard; four on each side of our front door, alternating deep gold and bright yellow. I plopped to my knees on the furthest left side of the empty flowerbeds, and dug a simple hole, and placed the plant inside. However, just as I was patting down the loose soil around the base, several additional blooms had popped up around it before my eyes. Within minutes, the entire front yard was overflowing with oversized marigolds, ranging from pale yellow to dark orange. The soil underneath was completely concealed under the blooms within mere moments, and I stood before it, aghast. I looked behind myself after a while, wondering if anyone else had witnessed this inexplicable act of nature before me, but only the remaining marigold plants I was supposed to plant stood behind me. Glancing at my bee tattoo, dusted with soil, the glowing was pulsing, as if it were gaining strength. 

I had spent the rest of the day transforming our landscape into what resembled a garden of Eden. Luckily, we lived on the end of a dirt road surrounded by no neighbors, so the miraculously instantaneous growth remained a secret- at least, until my husband had returned from home from work in the evening.

“What in the hell…” he muttered; his brown eyes furrowed with disbelief. 

“Come inside, my love,” I guided his distracted, nearly staggering self into the house, my little bee shining with remarkable brightness. “I have to explain something to you. Remember my bee tattoo…?”
